title: Landscape Construction: Technical Practices
description: Technical aspects of landscape construction projects. Building codes and legal criteria. Fences and gates. Landscape plan reading. Estimating landscape materials, construction costs, and preparation of project bids and contracts. Landscape surveying and grading techniques, surface and subsurface hydraulics, landscape drainage systems, erosion control, and soil conservation.
outcomes: Demonstrate, on manipulative examinations, the correct use of surveying tools used in landscape construction projects.
Demonstrate, on written examinations, knowledge of estimating techniques used in landscape construction.
objectives: Interpret building codes and legal restrictions related to landscape construction.
Read landscape construction documents (plans and specifications).
Demonstrate the correct use of surveying tools used in landscape construction projects and as applied to slopes and grading.
Identify landscape hydraulic and drainage systems.
Identify erosion control and soil conservation solutions.
content: Right of ways, easements, and set-backs
Identification of hardscape and softscape elements
Use of manual and electronic estimating tools
Laser plane, builders level, and transit
Surface and subsurface hydraulics and drainage
lab: Field practice in the use of surveying equipment on a residential lot
Field visits to witness drainage and grading applications
The application of grading as it applies to the proper drainage of a site
Following a lecture on plan reading, using a variety of landscape plans, students practice interpreting plans
Students use a variety of estimating equipment to develop cost estimates for a typical residential landscape
